states.name: INIT
states.description: Fresh instance before first scan. previousValue=0 and all outputs hold declared initial values.

states.name: RUN
states.description: Operational scan state. Each invocation samples value, computes edge masks/counts/flags, and updates previousValue after output calculation.

actions: compute risingBits and fallingBits using previousValue=0
compute risingBits and fallingBits using previousValue from prior scan

timer_plan.notes: No timers are required. All behavior is per-scan combinational with one retained previousValue state.

priorities: 1. Compute risingBits and fallingBits before updating previousValue; previousValue must be updated only after both edge masks are calculated.
2. Sample input value exactly once per scan and use that sampled value for all masks, counts, and flags.
3. Initialize previousValue to DWORD#0 so nonzero input bits on the first scan are reported as rising edges.
4. Derive noOfRisingBits and noOfFallingBits from the final risingBits and fallingBits masks using a 32-bit population count.
5. Derive hasRisingEdges, hasFallingEdges, and hasChanged from the current scan masks/value comparison, not from stale flags.
6. Keep all bitwise operations within unsigned 32-bit DWORD semantics.
7. No explicit reset is exposed by the interface; reset occurs only at instance initialization/first scan state.

scan_execution_order.name: edge sampling
actions: Sample input value once into an internal sampledValue variable.
Do not modify previousValue in this stage.

scan_execution_order.name: safety/reset priority and state transitions
actions: Apply instance-initialization behavior only before the first scan: previousValue remains 0 and outputs remain at initial values.
Transition INIT -> RUN on first invocation; RUN -> RUN on every later scan.
Preserve safety priority: previousValue must not be updated until both edge masks have been computed.

scan_execution_order.name: unconditional top-level timer FB calls outside CASE/IF
actions: No timer function blocks are used, so there are no timer calls to execute in this stage.
